newsitem.title: USA: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in Oct - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: U.S. adj retail sales up 0.2 pct in Oct - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.2 percent in the four weeks of fiscal October versus September, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 7.0 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 6.2 percent in the week ended November 2, compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
October sales were largely led by apparel, in contrast to last year, when hard lines boomed and soft lines struggled, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
"Apparel is selling. Apparel is leading the way," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Overall, October was a good month, said Eilenberg. The October results were a little better than expectations.
"Over the summer and even in September, retailers told us they were disappointed in results -- as far as their plans went. October is the present exception."
Looking forward to November, Eilenberg said the U.S. Presidential elections should have a positive impact on retail sales.
"If you look at previous elections, in those years, business tended to be pretty good," Eilenberg said, adding that "the economy is holding up better than we thought it would."
